# karpo-apple-silicon

> Unofficial community port that runs MachinePulse's Karpo Decision models (karpo-decision-31B and karpo-decision-12B, the Gemma 4 family checkpoints) on Apple Silicon Macs. One small PyTorch patch for the MPS (Metal) GPU, plus an experimental MLX path with 8-bit and 4-bit quantized weights. Apache-2.0. Not affiliated with MachinePulse or Google.

## The short answer

Karpo Decision as published needs an NVIDIA GPU. On a Mac the checkpoint loads, then the first `decide()` call fails with `NotImplementedError: The operator 'aten::_flash_attention_forward' is not currently implemented for the MPS device`, because the sliding-window layers call `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn`, which PyTorch only provides for CUDA. Calling `karpo_apple_silicon.install()` before the first `decide()` replaces that call with banded masked attention. Without CUDA it also lifts a global-layer kernel restriction that otherwise prevents CPU execution. The CPU forward was checked on a tiny random model only; no real checkpoint has been run on CPU. `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1` does not fix the original error.

## Install and use

```bash
pip install "karpo-decision @ git+https://github.com/machinepulse-ai/karpo-decision@6600011eb5cf46232d056ec0717dc726146d29de"
pip install "karpo-apple-silicon @ git+https://github.com/fluxcodestudio/karpo-apple-silicon"
```

```python
import karpo_apple_silicon
karpo_apple_silicon.install()
from karpo_decision.decider import Decider
decider = Decider.from_pretrained("path/to/karpo-decision-31B", device="mps")
```

## Facts

- Hardware: Apple Silicon Macs (M1, M2, M3, M4 and later), macOS 14 or later. Memory: about 96 GB for the 31B as shipped (62.6 GB of weights), more than 24.0 GB for the 12B.
- Less memory: the MLX path runs the 31B from quantized copies, 34.0 GB at 8 bits and 19.3 GB at 4 bits, text requests only.
- Ready-made MLX weights: https://huggingface.co/jonnyArt/karpo-decision-31B-mlx-8bit and https://huggingface.co/jonnyArt/karpo-decision-31B-mlx-4bit
- Accuracy against MachinePulse's published 31B results (340 requests, 1,606 questions): PyTorch on MPS changed 1 top answer (mean difference 0.0011); version 0.1.0 MLX 8-bit changed 2 (0.0016); version 0.1.0 MLX 4-bit changed 3 of 681 (0.0067). The reworked MLX loader and forward pass (version 0.2.0) have been checked on small random models, and both published folders have the required tensor names and shapes. On the real 4-bit weights version 0.2.0 gave the same top answer as version 0.1.0 on 71 questions (largest probability difference 0.061) with lower peak memory on long requests (23.3 GB to 20.9 GB at 7,464 tokens) and no measurable change in time; the 8-bit weights have not been run with version 0.2.0.
- Not covered or not checked: the Qwen-family Karpo models (0.8B to 9B and 27B-act), images, requests longer than 8,072 tokens, the 12B (no per-request results are published for it), GGUF / llama.cpp / Ollama. AMD and Intel GPUs have not been checked.
- Port version 0.2.0; tested with karpo-decision 0.1.0 (commit 6600011eb5cf), torch 2.15.0, transformers 5.23.0, mlx 0.32.4, mlx-lm 0.32.2. The installer compares pip's recorded upstream commit because the upstream version has not changed between commits, and checks the attention signature.
